name: Quetzalcoatl leaves Tula
traveler: Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl, priest-king of the Toltecs
summary: The Aztecs told how Tollan, the Toltec city of craftsmen, was ruled by a priest-king named for the Feathered Serpent. Tricked by the sorcerer Tezcatlipoca into drunkenness and shame, he burned his palaces, buried his treasures and walked east to the sea, where he set out on a raft of serpents or, some said, burned himself and rose as the morning star, promising to return. Landa heard in Yucatán that a lord called Kukulcan came from the west to Chichén Itzá, and the Toltec-style buildings there are often linked to the story. The tale is legend; the date is one reading of the year 1 Reed.

stops.note: Tollan's palaces of turquoise, shell and quetzal feathers. Shamed by Tezcatlipoca, he burns them and leaves.
He rests under a great tree and throws stones at it, which stay lodged in the trunk.
Cholula keeps him, some say for twenty years; it becomes the great shrine of Quetzalcoatl.
At the 'place where the serpent hides', on the Gulf shore, he sets out east on a raft of serpents for Tlillan Tlapallan.
A small island harbour on the north coast, the port of Chichén Itzá.
Landa's informants said Kukulcan, the Feathered Serpent, came from the west and ruled at Chichén Itzá.
